'''''Philotheca''''' is a [[genus]] of about fifty species of [[flowering plant]]s in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Rutaceae]]. Plants in this genus are shrubs with simple leaves arranged alternately along the stems, flowers that usually have five [[sepal]]s, five [[petal]]s and ten [[stamen]]s that curve inwards over the [[Ovary (botany)|ovary]]. All species are [[Endemism|endemic]] to Australia and there are species in every state, but not the Northern Territory.

==Description==
Plants in the genus ''Philotheca'' are shrubs that are either [[wikt:glabrous|glabrous]] or have tiny, simple hairs. The leaves are arranged alternately along the stems, narrow oblong to almost cylindrical and [[Sessility (botany)|sessile]] or on a very short [[Petiole (botany)|petiole]]. From a single to many flowers are arranged in leaf [[wikt:axil|axil]]s or on the ends of the branchlets. The flowers have five sepals and five petals (except in ''[[Philotheca virgata|P. virgata]]'' which has four). The sepals are free from each other and the petals usually overlap at their bases. There are ten stamens that curve inwards over the ovary with [[anthers]] that have an appendage called the "apiculum". The ovary contains five [[Gynoecium#Carpels|carpels]] fused near their bases. The seeds are {{cvt|2-5|mm}} long and are released explosively from their [[Capsule (botany)|capsule]].<ref name="ABRS">{{cite web |last1=Wilson |first1=Paul G. |title=''Philotheca'' |url=https://profiles.ala.org.au/opus/foa/profile/Philotheca |publisher=Australian Biological Resources Study, Department of the Environment and Energy, Canberra |accessdate=4 May 2019}}</ref><ref name="RBGV">{{cite web |last1=Walsh |first1=Neville |title=''Philotheca'' |url=https://vicflora.rbg.vic.gov.au/flora/taxon/9f35fef5-6e92-41fa-acd4-045346074a86 |publisher=Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria |accessdate=4 May 2019}}</ref><ref name="RBGS">{{cite web |last1=Weston |first1=Peter H. |last2=Harden |first2=Gwen J. |title=''Philotheca'' |url=http://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?page=nswfl&showsyn=&dist=&constat=&lvl=gn&name=Philotheca |publisher=Royal Botanic Garden Sydney |accessdate=4 May 2019}}</ref><ref name=FloraBase>{{FloraBase|name=''Philotheca''|id=22449}}</ref>

==Taxonomy and naming==
The genus ''Philotheca'' was first formally described in 1816 by [[Edward Rudge]] from a specimen collected near [[Port Jackson]] and the description was published in ''[[Linnean Society of London#Publications|Transactions of the Linnean Society of London]]''.<ref name=APNI>{{cite web|title=''Philotheca''|url= https://id.biodiversity.org.au/instance/apni/472579|publisher=APNI|accessdate=4 May 2019}}</ref><ref name="Rudge">{{cite journal |last1=Rudge |first1=Edward |title=A Description of several new Species of Plants from New Holland |journal=Transactions of the Linnean Society of London |date=1815 |volume=11 |issue=2 |page=298 |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/13721#page/327/mode/1up |accessdate=4 May 2019}}</ref> The first species Rudge described was ''P. australis'' but this name is considered a [[nomen illegitimum]] and a [[Synonym (taxonomy)|taxonomic synonym]] of ''[[Philotheca salsolifolia]]'' by the [[Australian Plant Census]].<ref name=APC2>{{cite web|title=''Philotheca salsolifolia''|url= https://biodiversity.org.au/nsl/services/apc-format/display/67404|publisher=Australian Plant Census|accessdate=4 May 2019}}</ref>

The name ''Philotheca'' should have been written ''Psilotheca'' after the [[Ancient Greek]] words ''psilos'' meaning "bare", "smooth", "bald" or "naked"<ref name="RWB">{{cite book|last1=Brown|first1=Roland Wilbur|title=The Composition of Scientific Words|date=1956|publisher=Smithsonian Institution Press|location=Washington, D.C.}}</ref>{{rp|123}} and ''theke'' meaning "case", "container", "envelope" or "sheath",<ref name ="RWB" />{{rp|118}} referring to "the smooth tube of the stamens".<ref name="Craig">{{cite book |last1=Craig |first1=John |title=A New Universal Etymological and Pronouncing Dictionary of the English Language embracing all the terms used in art, science and literature |date=1849 |publisher=Henry George Collins |location=London}}</ref>

Many plants formerly in ''[[Eriostemon]]'' are now in this genus.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://farrer.csu.edu.au/ASGAP/APOL13/mar99-3.html |first=Michael |last=Bayly |title=A Name Change for Most Eriostemons |work=Australian Plants online |date=March 1999
|publisher=The Society for Growing Australian Plants }}</ref>

==Distribution==
Plants in the genus ''Philotheca'' are found in every state of Australia, but not in the Northern Territory.<ref name="RBGS" />
